- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment turns positive sharply (e.g., > 0.70), model often overshoots upward; cap forecast peak at 1–2% below recent high or use moving average to smooth.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — increase baseline by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
- Model overestimates in late 30-day horizon when sentiment is positive — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- If recent 18-day price trend is rising and sentiment is positive, model often fails to capture momentum — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to reflect acceleration.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to lag — add 1–2 days of lag correction by shifting forecast 1–2 points higher for next period.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.30 → +0.70 → -0.40), model misreads trend direction — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth transitions.
